src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createApp sends every route's errors through next(error) to one error handler that maps ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError to 400/404/409

src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: readText, asObject, readQuery, readParam and readTaskInput are the single place where request input is checked; toTaskResponse is the single place where tasks are turned into responses
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createTaskService builds TaskService from the in-memory repositories (wiring kept beside the HTTP adapter)
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: the GET /projects/:projectId/tasks handler uses req.params.projectId directly instead of readParam (minor inconsistency)
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only calls createApp() and app.listen(port)
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module is one cohesive concern: the outer adapters that turn the Task API into a running program. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the storage adapters, which implement the domain repository interfaces. http-app.ts is the HTTP adapter: it reads and checks requests, maps errors to status codes in one handler and shapes task responses through toTaskResponse. It also has a small wiring function, createTaskService. server.ts is a minimal entry point. Each rule is written once: request checking in readText/asObject/readQuery/readParam, error-to-status mapping in the single error handler, response date formatting in toTaskResponse, and task filtering in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProjectId. No file reaches past TaskService into the repositories. Two minor points: the GET list handler reads req.params.projectId directly instead of using readParam, and the complete handler uses its own typeof check (justified, because projectId is optional on one of its two routes). Express always fills in matched route parameters, so neither duplicates a rule or bypasses the module's abstractions in a meaningful way.
